episodes.157792: Isolated but intense thunderstorms erupted during the midday hours, and lingered into the early evening hours. A few of the thunderstorms became severe, producing damaging winds.  A particularly strong downburst affected the southeast portion of Decatur, where dozens of homes were damaged, including fallen trees and power lines.  The Wheeler National Wildlife Refuge sustained significant tree fall damage.
episodes.157794: A cold front brought isolated late afternoon and evening severe storms that produced large hail, heavy rain and frequent lightning as well as isolated reports of damaging wind gusts.  The most severe weather occurred in Ovid in south central Michigan where baseball sized hail was reported in addition to several downed trees and power lines.
episodes.157797: An upper trough, surface trough, daytime heating, and sufficient atmospheric moisture led to numerous showers and thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening, a few of which reached severe limits.
episodes.157805: Scattered thunderstorms developed during the late afternoon and evening hours ahead of a cold front approaching the Ohio Valley Region.
episodes.157905: With an area of high pressure centered over southwest New Mexico, temperatures soared across northern and central portions of the state on June 12, 2021. Dry weather prevailed for most areas west of the Rio Grande Valley, but a cold front was responsible for drastically different weather conditions across the east. The cold front moved through eastern New Mexico late on June 11th and helped to replenish low-level moisture and provide an highly unstable and sheared environment. The result was a round of strong to severe thunderstorms that developed first over the northern high terrain and then moved east to southeast onto the plains. The strongest thunderstorm was a supercell near Las Vegas that produced very large hail up to three inches in diameter as well as a tornado. While the hail did some damage in the form of broken windshields, the tornado was over open country. As the thunderstorms marched towards the Texas border, the severe weather threat shifted to primarily a wind threat, and wind gusts exceeding 60 mph were recorded at several locations.
episodes.157919: Numerous afternoon thunderstorms developed across Brevard County, with many producing strong to severe wind gusts as they pushed offshore.
episodes.157920: A cluster of thunderstorms that developed in Brevard County produced severe wind gusts near Cape Canaveral. One of the storms produced a brief, weak tornado as it moved onshore from the Indian River and affected the Preserve Point subdivision in northwest Merritt Island.
episodes.157926: A stationary frontal boundary remained just north of the state on the 11th and first part of the day 12th, placing much of southeast Kentucky in the warm sector, and building instability. As this cold front quickly pushed southward during the afternoon hours on June the 12th, scattered storms developed. These storms became strong to severe as they moved into this unstable and untapped warm/moist airmass, leading to widespread wind damage across portions of the Jackson County Warning Area.
episodes.158377: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms moved across northern Illinois during the afternoon of June 12th producing sporadic hail and wind damage.  A more widespread area of wind damage occurred across portions of Iroquois County, where a brief gustnado was observed near Onarga.
episodes.158465: Several trees were blown down by wind gusts from a line of thunderstorms that tracked south across Rhea, Bradley, and Hamilton counties.
episodes.158473: A slow-moving cold front interacted with a highly unstable but weakly sheared environment to trigger scattered strong to severe thunderstorms across east-central Illinois during the late afternoon and early evening of June 12th.  Some of the storms produced wind gusts of around 60mph and caused minor wind damage.
episodes.158564: A slow moving low pressure system featured afternoon showers and thunderstorms over the span of a few days. A low level jet parked over the Ohio River Valley along with this moist airmass was the primary focus for rainfall, which resulted in several instances of flash flooding in West Virginia. The most substantial flooding took place near the town of Hamlin in Lincoln County, where twenty-five homes were damaged and two were destroyed due to a washed out culvert.
episodes.158650: A few thunderstorms developed during the early evening hours of June 11th.  One stronger storm briefly produced a damaging wind gust in northwestern Howard County as the core of the storm began to collapse.  No other storm caused any damage that day.
episodes.158701: A cold front moved across SE GA from the NE in the afternoon and became nearly stationary across the local forecast area near the GA/FL line. Aloft, upper level forcing rotated across the area within the base of an 500mb trough. The combination of diurnal heating, frontal convergence, and upper energy fueled numerous strong to severe storms across the local area.

episodes.159187: Severe thunderstorms producing strong winds and large hail moved across much of south central and southeast Kansas during the evening and overnight hours of June 11th, 2021.

episodes.159487: Thunderstorms moved southward across eastern Kansas and western Missouri during the day on the 11th, and continued into northeastern Oklahoma during the late evening hours. The strongest storm produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.159586: Strong to severe storms developed during the afternoon and evening ahead of a cold front approaching from the northwest. Numerous reports of wind gusts over 60 mph and damage to trees and powerlines occurred across portions of southwest Missouri.
episodes.159646: A line of thunderstorms tracked southward out of Kansas during the evening of the 11th and across much of central Oklahoma during the early morning hours of the 12th, producing numerous severe wind gusts and some localized damage.
episodes.159647: Scattered thunderstorms developed during the afternoon of the 13th, with a few severe wind reports received.
episodes.159683: Warm and unstable air in advance of a cold front led to thunderstorms developing across southeast Georgia and near Tybee Island Beach.
episodes.159684: Warm and unstable air in advance of a cold front and mid-level shortwave along with a sea breeze interacting with convective outflow boundaries led to severe thunderstorms across southeast South Carolina.
episodes.159735: Numerous showers and thunderstorms developed across Middle Tennessee during the afternoon hours on June 12th. Some storms became severe with several reports of wind damage, hail, and flash flooding.
episodes.159756: Isolated severe storms developed over central Lower Michigan on the afternoon and evening of June 12, 2021, including a long-lived supercell. This storm produced significant hail - some up to baseball-sized in Ovid, Michigan (Clinton County) - and a few instances of wind damage as it tracked from the Mt. Pleasant area all the way to Ann Arbor before dissipating in the late evening. Other clusters of storms developed in the evening over northern and central Lower Michigan, one of which tracked across Midland and Bay Counties and resulted in localized damaging wind gusts.
episodes.159867: Strong to severe storms developed during the afternoon and evening ahead of a cold front approaching from the northwest. Numerous reports of wind gusts over 60 mph and damage to trees and powerlines occurred across extreme southeastern Kansas.
episodes.159876: A weakening complex of storms moving south from Oklahoma produced a severe wind gust in Montague County and hail in Collin County.
episodes.159978: An isolated thunderstorm developed in a weakly sheared, slightly unstable environment in southern Lower Michigan. Isolated wind damage occurred during the collapse stage of the storm.
episodes.159986: An isolated thunderstorm developed in a weakly sheared, slightly unstable environment in southern Lower Michigan. The Three Rivers airport recorded a 66 mph wind gusts with a collapsing storm. No reports of damage were received.

episodes.160043: The upper air pattern transitioned from west to northwest flow across Alabama during this time period.  Deep moisture with PWAT's above 1.8 inches combined with increasing mid level lapse rates to create favorbale conditions for heavy rainfall and strong thunderstorm winds.
episodes.160134: A typical summertime pattern prevailed with a few strong thunderstorms producing wind gusts in excess of 34 knots.
episodes.160145: Central Kentucky sat under the leading edge of an upper ridge during a period of typical summer weather.  Temperatures rose during the day creating strong instability in the atmosphere that caused showers and thunderstorms to breakout. As rain filled downdrafts initiated outflow boundaries, the outflow boundaries initiated more storms. This happened daily before a weak cold front pushed drier air into the region. Several counties in central Kentucky received isolated wind damage during this three day stretch. Scott County had flooding issues on June 13th.
episodes.160157: Widely scattered thunderstorms developed during the afternoon of June 11th in an environment of strong afternoon heating as temperatures warmed into the low to mid 80s ahead of a backdoor cold front draped across northern Virginia. CAPE values were in excess of 2,000 J/Kg and Precipitable Water values were observed to be in the 1.8 to 1.9 inch range. Weak atmospheric winds resulted in slow storm motion.  The combination of deep instability and abundant moisture resulted in storms producing high rainfall rates of 2 to locally 5 inches per hour, with 1-hour rainfall totals exceeding 3.2 inches near the City of Lynchburg.  This rainfall is a 100-year event per NOAA Atlas 14 Point Precipitation Frequency estimates.  One swift water rescue was reported in the City of Lynchburg when a vehicle was stranded in the floodwaters from Blackwater Creek.  No injuries were reported.
episodes.160440: Scattered thunderstorms along a frontal boundary produced heavy rain which caused flash flooding across portions of central and eastern Virginia.
episodes.160597: Multiple rounds of storms initiated near the I-75 corridor during the afternoon and evening, producing severe hail in several counties across the area.
episodes.160613: Daytime heating led to large amounts of instability and a few strong to severe storms across West Tennessee with some hail and damaging winds during the afternoon and evening on June 12, 2021.
